Week notesWhat you worked out

Use the weekly transfer prompt and teach-back with your Fercaf thesis as the running case: record (1) your explanation from memory, (2) a calculation with units and an explicitly stated interpretation, (3) an assumption or limitation, and (4) what measurement would distinguish competing metabolic explanations. Mark unmeasured biology as unknown. Check thesis conclusions against its reported data and criteria, including the whiteness result and water-to-substrate ratio notation. Open the source-audited case study · Weekly transfer prompts.

How the quiz picksSpaced recall

Eight items a day, drawn from every week up to your active one. Answer one correctly and it moves to a longer box — 2 days, then 5, 12, 25, 60, 120, then retired. Miss it and it returns tomorrow at the first interval. Multiple choice is graded for you; written recall you grade yourself against the model answer, strictly. Recognising an answer is not knowing it.

Eleven-point protocolLog a paper

Fill this in for every paper you read closely. If a reading map gives only an author and title, resolve the full reference and DOI before you log it — the log is only as good as its provenance. Forty entries is the target by week 46, one a week from week 7; points 8 to 10 are the ones most applicants cannot answer and the ones your degree lets you answer well.

Localization and transport

Two questions to answer for every paper. Where the product sits decides the host, the toxicity problem and the whole downstream train.

Editions used, and what to check

Chapter numbering changes between editions. If you use a different printing, find the section by title and record the edition in your notes. Check for a newer edition before buying; the primary literature is the authority where the two disagree.

TextEdition used, and what to check
Berg, Tymoczko & Stryer, Biochemistry7th edn (2012) is the printing the chapter pointers were checked against. Check for the current edition; chapter numbering moves.
Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the CellEdition not stated in the maps. Check the current edition and locate sections by title, not number.
OpenStax, MicrobiologyOnline edition; check the revision date before citing a section.
Shuler & Kargi, Bioprocess Engineering2nd edn (2002). Check for a current edition.
Stanbury, Whitaker & Hall, Principles of Fermentation Technology2nd edn (1995) is the printing used. A 3rd edn (2016) exists and its chapter numbering differs; if you use it, find the section by title.
Nielsen, Stephanopoulos & Lee (eds.), Metabolic Engineering2021, Wiley-VCH. doi:10.1002/9783527823468. The field's current multi-author reference; pair it with current reviews for anything method-specific.
Palsson, Systems Biology: COBRA2015. The uploaded extract covers chapters 1–3; the full book is the reference for the rest.
Doran, Bioprocess Engineering PrinciplesThe maps point at chapters by number; check which edition your copy is and locate by title.
Belter, Bioseparations; Plawsky, Transport Phenomena Fundamentals; Smith, Van Ness & Abbott, Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics; Voet, Fundamentals of BiochemistryCheck the current edition of each before buying; the chapter pointers are to the printing named in the briefs' book list.

HoursLog a session

Target is about 44 hours a week across five days: twelve sessions of three to four hours. Roughly half primary reading and derivation, a third problem-solving and coding, the rest literature and writing.
